newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF survey shows economy recovering slowly.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF survey shows economy recovering slowly.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing to show gradual improvement, a Ministry of Finance quarterly corporate survey showed on Tuesday.
"Japan's economy is continuing to recover, but the tempo is gradual. Private-sector demand, such as corporate capital spending, is becoming stronger," a MOF official told reporters.
The quarterly survey, conducted in early November, asked 10,096 companies how they viewed business conditions for the October-December period.

A higher number of medium- and large-sized companies thought the economy was improving this quarter compared with the previous period, but more small companies thought the economy was worsening, the survey showed.
The survey also showed a further rise in the number of companies which expect brighter economic prospects in the January to March period.

However, there was a slight decline in the number of companies which thought the economy would continue to improve in the April to June quarter, partly due to the rise in the consumption tax from April 1997, the MOF official said.

They expected profits in the current business year to next March 31 to rise 13 percent from the year before. In MOF's last quarterly survey, the companies estimated an 18.2 percent rise from the previous year.

Companies which saw rises in profits attributed the increases to better sales and cuts in labour costs. Lower sales and prices and an increase in labour costs were the reasons cited by companies that saw profits fall, the survey said.
It also showed that big corporations, especially manufacturers, still had too many workers.
